deepdive.sec: Financial Services — Small Finance Bank (retail-secured-led, transitioning toward universal bank)

bull_bear.body: No dividend/buyback/raise discussed. Capital is being deployed into (a) distribution — 100+ branches, (b) technology ~₹1,000cr p.a., and (c) balance-sheet growth at 2-2.5x nominal GDP. Funding-side allocation choices: within bulk deposits the bias is toward **non-callable** TDs (stable deposits 79% of total), and FCNR rates were raised to ~7.4-7.5% opportunistically rather than to a target. On the CD ratio, Sanjay Agarwal explicitly refused to treat it as an optimisation variable: "*CD ratio ex-refinance is ~80%. So we don't look this number to optimize anything.*"
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **ECL transition is un-quantified.** Every other large bank is putting a number on transition and steady-state credit-cost impact; AU declined twice, saying models are preliminary and the outcome depends on Board-approved accelerated-provisioning and write-off policies. Their claim of neutrality rests on the Stage-3 cushion covering Stage-1/2 build. **Deferred to end-Q3 — a hard date to hold them to.**
- **NIM has no guidance and cost of funds has bottomed.** With savings and wholesale rates already raised and the mix shifting toward lower-yield secured/gold assets, the ROA bridge to 1.8% now depends entirely on opex leverage, credit cost and a hoped-for other-income recovery — three soft levers.
- **Unsecured recovery is early and low-base.** PL +19% QoQ and MFI +5% QoQ are off depressed bases; credit card is still loss-making. Management refused to give unsecured growth targets ("*industry has just started to revive after almost six to eight quarters of degrowth*").
- **Commercial banking NPA uptick QoQ** in the SME/business-banking book — described as a normal Q1 seasonal pattern that "slows down" later; worth verifying in Q2.
- **NSFR structurally lower than pre-2024** (108-109 vs 115-120+ historically) — management's answer was simply "that's the range we operate," with no explanation of why the range reset.
- **MFI is deliberately not an ROA engine** — capped at 10% of book and run for PSL/small-and-marginal-farmer obligation. Growth there is compliance-driven, so it should not be extrapolated as a profit lever.
- **Succession is now an explicit board project.** Sanjay Agarwal spoke unprompted about not having "infinite years" — constructive, but it is a governance transition to monitor.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, specific and notably willing to say "no." Gaurav Jain refused to give NIM guidance and corrected an analyst who inferred one ("*we haven't guided for stable, there's no guidance on NIM*"); Vivek Tripathi twice declined to quantify ECL rather than offering a soft number; Prince Tiwari pushed back on judging credit-card/PL risk-adjusted yields at this stage and conceded plainly that credit cards are loss-making. Sanjay Agarwal was candid on the ROA gap ("*we are just looking a 10 bps from here… it's not that big difference from our stated target*") and unusually open on leadership succession, framing the elevation of Yogesh Jain as deliberate, unhurried institution-building rather than a reaction. The overall register is a bank that believes it is past its unsecured credit cycle and is now selling durability rather than a growth story.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Headcount fell month-on-month for the first time (April→May) because of AI, not a hiring freeze** — and management linked it to a second-order effect that matters for cost structure: banking roles that previously could not be remote can now be done "from home or anywhere." A cost-to-assets improvement driven by structural back-office automation is a very different quality of operating leverage than one driven by growth outpacing fixed costs.
- **The MFI business model has changed shape, not just improved.** Buffer-building has been replaced by a paid guarantee (CGFMU on 96% of the book), so the credit-cost line is now a premium expense with far less variance — the reported credit-cost improvement is partly a *form* change, and Sanjay Agarwal was explicit that economically "*it's a similar thing. You pay credit cost now. Guarantee cost now.*"
- **Renewable-energy lending is a quiet, policy-driven niche** built over three years inside commercial banking — PM-KUSUM Component A/C, 2-5MW developer projects — where the credit case rests on the capital subsidy plus attractive discom PPAs, not on the renewable theme itself.
- **CGFMU coverage on GNPA is materially lower than on the live book** (96%) because a chunk of current NPAs originate from vintage, pre-coverage pools — so the guarantee provides less protection against *already-recognised* stress than the headline suggests.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital position stated as Tier I capital ratio 17.1% and total CRAR 18.9% (vs 18.2% / 20.0% in Q1'FY26 and 16.9% / 18.7% in Q4'FY26); "RWA to Total Assets stands at ~61% as on 30th Jun'26".
- Balance sheet at 30th Jun'26: Shareholders Fund ₹20,885 cr (+17% YoY), Deposits ₹1,57,727 cr (+24%), Borrowings ₹13,419 cr (+26%), Total Assets ₹1,97,125 cr (+23%); BVPS ₹279 vs ₹239 a year ago.
- Funding discipline: CD ratio 88% at Jun'26 vs 86% at Jun'25, and 80% excluding loans against which refinance was availed from domestic DFIs (vs 79% at Jun'25); average LCR 119% for the quarter, with "additional liquidity equivalent to 10-15% of LCR in the form of high-quality, liquid, non-LCR investments".
- Provisioning buffer disclosed at Jun'26: total provisions ₹2,438 cr, i.e. "Provisions as a % of gross advances" of 1.74% (vs 1.69% at Mar'26), including contingency provisions ₹37 cr, floating provisions ₹41 cr and standard asset provisions ₹476 cr.
- Credit ratings: AA/Stable (long term / subordinated debt / Tier II bonds, CRISIL/CARE/ICRA), A1+ short term (CRISIL/CARE/India Ratings) and AA+/Stable on Fixed Deposits (CRISIL).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Retail secured (67% of loan book):** +23% YoY, +4% QoQ.
  - **Wheels:** ₹48,600cr, +28% YoY, +5% QoQ — new-vehicle demand strong, traction in newer geographies (South, UP, East).
  - **Gold loans:** ₹4,500cr, **+130% YoY, +15% QoQ** — Fincare-inherited capability scaled into AU's North-West distribution; >80% rural, avg ticket ~₹2.5 lakh (majority <₹5 lakh), portfolio IRR ~15.5%.
  - **Mortgages** (micro-business loans + affordable housing): +12% YoY, +2% QoQ — the laggard, but **disbursements +28% YoY**, i.e. the book is inflecting.
- **Commercial banking:** ₹32,800cr, +34% YoY, +6% QoQ, broad-based across sub-verticals; strategy is to make it progressively self-funded via current accounts + transaction banking/CMS/trade. **Renewable-energy book +120%+ YoY** — lending to PM-KUSUM Component A/C developers, typical project 2-5MW, concentrated in Rajasthan then Gujarat/Maharashtra/MP; attraction is favourable PPAs plus capital subsidy improving project viability. SME/business-banking book drove the small QoQ uptick in commercial-banking NPAs (seasonal Q1 pattern).
- **Inclusive banking (MFI):** +15% YoY, +5% QoQ; collection efficiency **99.5%** (only ~20bps below Q4, vs a normally seasonal Q1 dip); **96% of the book covered by CGFMU** guarantee.
- **Digital unsecured:** +3% YoY, +7% QoQ. Personal loans +24% YoY, +19% QoQ off a low base — **100% cross-sell to existing bank customers (99% ETB)**, scorecard/analytics-driven; credit card marginal growth, still loss-making, PL at/around breakeven.
- **Liabilities, four verticals:** branch banking 60% of deposits; government & interbank 21%; commercial banking & wholesale 7%; FIG 8%. New zero-forex-margin/zero-charge international retail remittance product launched (claimed a first among Indian private banks).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **CGFMU guarantee coverage on 96% of the MFI book** structurally converts a volatile credit-cost line into a predictable premium: "*instead of building up the buffers, we are securing protection on that book*" (Gaurav Jain) — this is why the steady-state MFI credit-cost assumption drops from 3% to ~2.5% with far lower variance.
- **Low LGDs on a 67%-secured retail book**, which management leans on as the reason the ECL transition should be P&L-neutral: "*our retail secured asset and even on the commercial side, it's largely secured. Our LGDs are pretty low compared to what the industry would look like.*"
- **Cross-sell moat on the liability base** — the entire restarted PL book is sourced from existing (99% ETB) customers with transaction-scorecard underwriting, i.e. growth without new-to-bank risk.
- **Fincare-acquired capability** (gold-loan operating ecosystem: valuers, ops, origination + an experienced MFI team) is being redeployed into AU's own distribution — a genuine acquisition synergy rather than balance-sheet addition.

business.body:
- Framed as "AU SFB: Scaled, profitable, with 'in-principle' approval for Universal Bank" - "Founded in 1996 as a vehicle financier, AU built strong capabilities in serving underserved, self-employed customers across semi-urban and rural India; Over the last nine years, AU has evolved into India's largest SFB with strong governance and risk management track record".
- Headroom argument: "~0.7/0.6% market share -> significant runway across loans and deposits respectively" with "Strong positioning in underpenetrated underserved retail, MSME and informal segments" (market share computed on RBI weekly supplement data as on 30th Jun'26).
- Business-model claim: "A scaled, retail loan book which is largely secured (>90%), well diversified (10+ business lines) with a pan-India distribution (~2900 touchpoints) having best-in-class, through the cycle risk adjusted yields; underpinned by a strong and granular deposits franchise built from ground up".
- Stated cross-cycle record: "Deposits and advances CAGR at 45% and 34% respectively, with avg RoA of 1.6% and avg RoE of 14.2% over the last 9 years"; a footnote adds "*Including exceptional items, 9 year average RoA is at 1.8% and RoE at 15.7%".
- Governance framing: "Stable, founder-led leadership with institutionalized governance" and a "Deep leadership bench of young talent with ~10 years average tenure with AU"; the 'Right to Win' is stated as "Customer insight x Distribution x Digital x UB transition (in-principle approval)".

Independent Directors), Domestic Institutions, Individuals and Others - the extract does not preserve which percentage binds to which holder, so the split is not asserted.

business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- NIM 5.9%, +47bps YoY but -7bps QoQ; cost of funds flat at 6.48% as higher SA/wholesale costs offset residual retail-TD repricing. Management says cost of funds has **bottomed**, so NIM defence now depends on asset mix, not liability repricing.
- Credit cost (incl. CGFMU fee) 0.8% vs 1.4% — the single largest driver of ROA improvement.
- Cost-to-assets 4.0% ex-CGFMU (vs 3.9%); opex +26% YoY but **-1% QoQ**, and **headcount actually declined in May — the first monthly decline** — attributed to AI absorbing back-office (operations, accounts, finance) work while front-line hiring continues.
- Technology spend ~**₹1,000cr, ~12-13% of total opex**.
- Product-level profitability disclosure declined: credit card explicitly **loss-making**, PL "around breakeven" — management asked for time before being held to product ROAs. Credit-card yield is subdued because the revolve share fell after underwriting tightening ~18 months ago.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** PAT ₹796cr (+37% YoY) on PPOP +41%; NIM 5.9% (+47bps YoY, -7bps QoQ); credit cost 0.8% (vs 1.4%); ROA 1.7% / ROE 15.6%; deposits ₹1.58 lakh cr (+24%), loans +23%, disbursements +42%; slippages ₹798cr (-22% YoY); one-time ₹23cr provisioning-alignment charge. Unsecured cycle turned (MFI +5% QoQ, PL +19% QoQ). Gold ₹4,500cr (+130%), wheels ₹48,600cr (+28%), commercial banking ₹32,800cr (+34%), mortgages the laggard at +12%. Yogesh Jain elevated to Deputy CEO; CRO-designate and Head of Technology appointed. Guidance: ROA target 1.8%, growth 2-2.5x nominal GDP, 100+ deposit branches this year, cost-to-assets to improve full-year, ECL impact "neutral" with colour promised by end-Q3, MFI capped at 10% of book at ~2.5% credit cost.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: whether commercial-banking NPA uptick reverses as claimed (seasonal); ROA closing the 10bps gap to 1.8%; cost-to-assets trending below 4.0%; branch additions tracking to 100+; CGFMU claims lodged by end-Q2; NIM direction now that cost of funds has bottomed; mortgage book converting its +28% disbursement growth into book growth; whether headcount decline persists (AI operating leverage) or reverses._
- _Q3 FY27 → hard checkpoint: management promised ECL transition + steady-state credit-cost quantification "by end of Q3."_
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Loan/franchise growth:** compound at **2.0-2.5x India's nominal GDP growth** — framed as a 10-year run-rate, not a one-year number.
- **ROA:** stated target **1.8%** (currently 1.7%). Management explicitly declined a NIM guide; the ~10bps bridge is to come from **opex and credit cost improving vs full-FY26**, plus a recovery in other income "in the next 6 to 9 months."
- **Margin:** *no NIM guidance given.* Directional: cost of funds has **bottomed out**, will be "stable to maybe increasing a little bit"; asset yields will reflect mix.
- **Cost-to-assets:** guided to **improve on a full-year basis** vs the 4.0% Q1 print, as operating leverage plays out.
- **Distribution:** **100+ additional deposit branches** to be added this year (16 added in Q1).
- **ECL transition:** management expects the impact to be **neutral** given low historical LGDs/PDs and existing Stage-3 provisioning cushion; refuses to quantify now, promises **"some colors by end of Q3."**
- **MFI/inclusive banking:** book capped at **up to 10% of the total loan book** (PSL/small-and-marginal-farmer obligation driven, not an ROA driver). Steady-state MFI credit cost re-rated from the old 3% assumption to **~2.5%** now that the CGFMU guarantee cost replaces buffer-building.
- **CGFMU claims:** claims on the crystallised FY26 NPA pool to be **lodged by end-Q2 FY27 and realised by mid-to-end December 2026**.
- **FCNR:** no specific mobilisation target — deliberately declined ("*we are not targeting now a specific one because if you don't have a leverage, it's difficult to convince the customer*").
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Not applicable in the conventional sense (bank). Pipeline proxies: **disbursements +42% YoY** in a seasonally soft quarter; new CASA acquisition with **80% YoY growth in premium accounts**; **>1 lakh new credit cards** issued in Q1; gold-loan product extended to 400+ additional branches taking distribution to **1,300+ branches**; pre-approved PL offers up **>3x** from propensity models.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Gold loans (₹4,500cr, +130%), renewable-energy project finance (+120%), transaction banking/forex (income +46% YoY) and the re-started personal-loan/credit-card engines are the four optionality legs. The structural one is geography: the bank was a North-West franchise until ~2 years ago and — post-Fincare and via deeper UP/Bihar/East/South buildout — now describes itself as pan-India, with the explicit claim that a full-India franchise is what makes the 2-2.5x-nominal-GDP compounding credible for a decade.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: A clean, broad-based beat: PAT +37% YoY to ₹796cr on core PPOP +41%, NIM up 47bps YoY to 5.9%, credit cost halved to 0.8% and ROA/ROE at 1.7%/15.6% — with loan growth (23%) and deposit growth (24%) both running well ahead of the private-bank system (17%/14%). The strategic story this quarter is that the unsecured cycle has turned (slippages -22% YoY, MFI +5% QoQ, PL +19% QoQ) just as the bank's newer geographies and newer products (gold +130% YoY, renewable-energy financing +120% YoY) start contributing — leaving management ~10bps short of its stated 1.8% ROA target and unusually relaxed about the pending ECL transition.

verdicts.note: We are working to increase our productivity in newer geographies like Andhra, Karnataka, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, and UP.

verdicts.item: FY26 loan growth targeted at 2x-2.5x nominal GDP, with heavy lifting from vehicle finance, commercial banking and gold loans (each ~20%-25%).
verdicts.note: Loan portfolio grew by 8% Q-o-Q and 21% Y-o-Y.

verdicts.item: Aiming to lift mortgages growth from ~15% to 17%-18% this year and to 20%+ in subsequent years; competitive intensity is a downside risk.
verdicts.note: Our mortgages business comprising micro business loan and affordable housing grew by 11% year-on-year to approximately ₹42,400 crores.

verdicts.item: Plan to add ~70-80 new deposit branches this year, mostly in the top cities.
verdicts.note: We are opening 80 to 100 newer branches every year. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: MBL branch network (924 in March '25) to increase by another 200-plus branches in FY26.
verdicts.note: In the last two years, we have nearly doubled our retail asset distribution to about 900 to 1,000 branches for each of our retail secured businesses.

verdicts.item: Wheels distribution to expand by another 200-plus branches in FY26 (from 715 in March '25), a ~70% increase over March '24.
verdicts.note: In the last two years, we have nearly doubled our retail asset distribution to about 900 to 1,000 branches for each of our retail secured businesses.

verdicts.item: Q2 FY26 expected to be the bottom for NIM (5.4% in Q1), with gradual improvement from Q3 onwards assuming no further rate cuts.
verdicts.note: Margins expanded by 24 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 5.96%.

wtt.summary: 63% guidance hit (53 chains); 9/9 projects on-time; 7 expired; 17% theme consistency (info)

meta.thesis: A clean, broad-based beat: PAT +37% YoY to ₹796cr on core PPOP +41%, NIM up 47bps YoY to 5.9%, credit cost halved to 0.8% and ROA/ROE at 1.7%/15.6% — with loan growth (23%) and deposit growth (24%) both running well ahead of the private-bank system (17%/14%). The strategic story this quarter is that the unsecured cycle has turned (slippages -22% YoY, MFI +5% QoQ, PL +19% QoQ) just as the bank's newer geographies and newer products (gold +130% YoY, renewable-energy financing +120% YoY) start contributing — leaving management ~10bps short of its stated 1.8% ROA target and unusually relaxed about the pending ECL transition.
